calls.reason: The 2026 Nature paper shows hallucinations persist in top models, but OpenAI's research argues abstention could avoid them. No proof of impossibility exists and no fix has been shown, so this open-ended claim can't be called yet.

Sora launched publicly on Dec 9, 2024, and the packet shows no major legal fight at launch. The only formal rights-holder action found is CODA's written request about Sora 2, sent ten months later, which was a letter and not litigation.

The only possible counterexample is the Dukaan CEO's interview claim of support-cost savings, which shows no reconciled profit effect. A search that finds no other company can't confirm the claim either, so the evidence is too thin.

Be My AI testimonials and Microsoft's survey of selected early Copilot users show some real benefits, but neither measures how widespread they were. The claim's qualitative 'few if any' can't be settled on this evidence.
This is a conditional forecast and its trigger hasn't happened. J.P. Morgan's October 2026 report shows AI still drawing over 80% of venture funding, not a collapse.
OpenAI's own update confirms some tasks got worse but says most metrics improved, and the Stanford study found mixed changes. No consistent time series shows whether overall progress slowed.
